IUI involves placing washed, concentrated sperm directly into the uterus around the time of ovulation, giving sperm a head start toward the egg compared to natural conception. A failed embryo transfer produces clinical data — how the endometrium developed, how embryos graded at day 5, whether transfer was technically straightforward — and all of it informs what should change in the next cycle. PGT-A screens blastocyst embryos for chromosomal abnormalities before transfer by biopsying 5–10 cells from the trophectoderm — the layer that forms the placenta rather than the embryo itself. The IVF Centre in Malad at Saraogi Hospital & IRIS IVF Centre applies PGT-A selectively based on case history, not as a default add-on for every patient.
